name: Eminence EMN claim/award bypasses bonding-curve reserve accounting
summary: EminenceCurrency prices buy() and sell() on a Bancor curve over totalSupply and reserveBalance, but its gamemaster functions claim() and award() burn and mint EMN without touching the reserve. eAAVE, a gamemaster, calls them. Under a flash loan the attacker bought EMN, burned half into eAAVE to lift EMN's price, sold, minted it back and sold again.
notes: EMN is immutable; the exploit needed eAAVE's gamemaster grant on EMN, which eAAVE's constructor obtained through addGM's tx.origin check, so that grant (rule 10) sets the age rather than EMN's deployment shortly before. eAAVE uses the API as intended and is not a separate target.

Loss nets DAI in and out of EMN per transaction, so flash-loan principal repaid inside each transaction is not counted; DAI is at its DefiLlama price. The 8M DAI the attacker returned is a recovery and is not subtracted.
The deployment was unannounced and unfinished but live and permissionless, holding user deposits.
